caveat_refs.quote: Higher is better except for NutriBench macro MAE, where lower is better.
The metric results are averaged over 8 parent-SFT model pairs for mathematics, 8 for coding, and 3 for nutrition.
† denotes joint-capability settings, where the same queries require both fine-tuned and general capabilities.
For nutrition models, we use IFEval as a proxy for non-food queries, and we refer to this as NutriBench-Non-Food.

no_rule_reason: The claim states specific numerical gaps between columns (SFT vs. SFT-as-Context on AIME 2024, LiveCodeBench, and NutriBench-English) and an average gap across rows between columns (Parent vs. SFT-as-Context across General Capabilities rows), as well as counts of model pairs (19, listed in Table 4 and only summarized as 8+8+3 in Table 1's caption) and benchmarks (11, where NutriBench is split into 3 subset names in Table 1 giving 13 distinct Benchmark labels across 17 data rows). None of the allowed rules (all_cmp, beats_baseline, best_in_column, count_rows, count_satisfying) can express arithmetic differences between two columns or averages of column differences across multiple rows.
